record.original_question: In coherent diffraction imaging or ptychography, can one estimate how complex an unknown object is using only its magnitude-only measurements, for example by using existing complexity statistics or by defining new ones that are computable from the measurements before reconstruction?

evidence.quote: Questions 3.1. 1. What are the current practices and what measures could be used for estimating the object’s complexity from the measurements?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the setting of coherent diffraction imaging (CDI) and ptychography. An unknown complex-valued object $O:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{C}$ is illuminated by one or more coherent probes, and the detector records only the squared magnitudes of the resulting far-field (Fraunhofer) diffraction patterns. In CDI a single magnitude measurement $I(\mathbf{q})=|\mathcal{F}\{P\cdot O\}(\mathbf{q})|^2$ is collected, where $\mathcal{F}$ denotes the Fourier transform and $P$ is the illumination function; in ptychography a set of such measurements $\{I_j(\mathbf{q})=|\mathcal{F}\{P(\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{r}_j)\cdot O(\mathbf{r})\}(\mathbf{q})|^2\}_j$ is collected over overlapping probe positions $\{\mathbf{r}_j\}$.

Define the "complexity" of the object $O$ as a quantitative measure of its structural intricacy (for example, its information content, sparsity in some basis, total variation, effective number of degrees of freedom, or any other statistic capturing how difficult $O$ is to represent or reconstruct). 

Problem: Identify or design a statistic $\mathcal{C}$ that takes as input only the magnitude-only measurements $\{I_j\}$ (i.e., is computable directly from the diffraction data, before any phase-retrieval reconstruction of $O$) and provides a reliable estimate of the complexity of the underlying object $O$. Equivalently, determine which existing complexity statistics defined on objects can be approximated, or which new statistics can be defined, purely from the recorded intensities, and analyze their relationship to standard object-domain complexity measures.
artifact.category_tag: Phase retrieval and coherent diffraction imaging
artifact.status_search_result: No established statistic for estimating object complexity directly from magnitude-only CDI/ptychography measurements (prior to reconstruction) was found in the literature. Existing work focuses on reconstructing the object and then assessing its complexity, rather than predicting complexity from raw intensity data. The question appears to be an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Computational microscopy with coherent diffractive imaging and ptychography
status_evidence.snippet: Review of CDI and ptychography reconstruction methods; complexity is discussed post-reconstruction, not estimated from raw magnitudes.
status_evidence.claim: Current practice estimates object properties after phase retrieval, not directly from magnitude measurements.

status_evidence.title: Ptychography: A solution to the phase problem
status_evidence.snippet: Describes use of magnitude constraints in iterative phase retrieval to reconstruct the complex object.
status_evidence.claim: Standard pipelines reconstruct the object first; no pre-reconstruction complexity measure is standard.
